_about: Shared by build_marks.py and the Course Planner page, so a report drafts the same text wherever it is built.

analysis.lead: {met}% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of {target}%, and {below}% did not meet them. The class averaged {average}% on this CLO.

below: Did this CLO get enough class time for its weight in the assessment?
Did students practise this kind of task before it was graded?
Was {item} a fair test of this CLO, and did students know what a good answer looks like?
When did students first get feedback on this CLO, and was that early enough to act on?
near: Who sits just below the Meet line, and what would have moved them over it?
Which session on this CLO would I teach differently next time?
Did {item} show what students can do, or did it catch them out?
above: What worked here that I should keep, or use for a weaker CLO?
Was the assessment demanding enough for the strongest students?
Does anything in this result come from the marking rather than the learning?

higher: Add two graded practice cases on {item} before the assessment, with a worked model answer and the rubric shared in advance.
Replace one lecture with a guided case discussion where students defend a decision, then give written feedback within a week.
Run a short diagnostic after the first sessions and hold a support clinic for students below the Meet line.
lower: Add short weekly quizzes on {item}, with answers reviewed at the start of the next class.
Reteach the core method with worked examples, then set a low-stakes practice before the assessment.
Run peer study circles for students below the Meet line ahead of the assessment.

higher: Add one more practice case on {item}, and share two sample answers at different rubric levels.
Give students feedback on a draft before the final submission for this CLO.
lower: Add a revision session on {item} before the assessment.
Give an early low-stakes check, so that students near the Meet line know where they stand.

higher: Keep the current approach, and add a stretch task for students who already exceed expectations.
Share what worked on this CLO with colleagues teaching related subjects.
lower: Keep the current approach, and raise the Bloom's level of {item} so the CLO is tested in more depth.
